title: PPS as the space of the bodily self
citation: Noel, J.-P., Pfeiffer, C., Blanke, O., & Serino, A. (2015). Peripersonal space as the space of the bodily self. Cognition, 144, 49-57.
notes: Audio-tactile PPS task intermingled with full-body-illusion stroking. This proxy profile captures the front-space main PPS trial schedule with chest vibration and source-backed synchronous/asynchronous stroking block labels. The separate back-space experiment still needs its own back-space/back-tactile variant before the full front/back expected-outcome contrast can be compared. A 100-ms derived terminal margin contains the existing software cue; it is not a reported trial interval or evidence of full-protocol timing equivalence.

reference_parameters.software_trial_padding_basis: Derived containment for the existing software timeline: pre=0 ms; post=max(0,max(SOA)+cue duration-source duration)=1140+100-1140=100 ms. Noel et al. 2015 Methods 2.3.2 and 2.4: the last reported sound-relative cue is 1140 ms and lasts 100 ms; exact sound offset is unreported. The current 1.14-s premade clip is a software choice. The reported 0.5-s inter-trial interval and 10-s FBI period after each triplet are separate protocol requirements, not demonstrated by this containment margin.

provenance.source: Methods lines report 72 PPS trials, 24 baseline trials, and 12 catch trials per block.
Methods lines report six sound distances D6-D1 with tactile timing corresponding to the spatial dimension.
Manual review records synchronous and asynchronous visuo-tactile stroking as separate counterbalanced blocks for the front-space chest-vibration experiment.
